variables.$BASE_URL: runtime: http://127.0.0.1:<port> of the fake server (from the LISTENING line)
variables.$STORAGE_DIR: runtime: a fresh absolute path per scenario whose parent exists and which does not exist yet
variables.$MINTED_SESSION_TOKEN: runtime: sessionToken returned by the most recent mintSession step
variables.$UNREACHABLE_BASE_URL: runtime: GET /__control/unreachable -> baseUrl (fetch once per scenario, before the first step)
variables.$NOW: runtime: current UTC time, ISO-8601, evaluated when the step starts

scenarios.title: No targets is a configuration error
scenarios.description: Constructing an SDK instance without any target throws invalid_config synchronously, before any I/O.

scenarios.title: Malformed targets are configuration errors
scenarios.description: Logins/slugs that violate the PROTOCOL §1 patterns throw invalid_config when the instance is constructed.

scenarios.title: Targets are trimmed, lowercased and canonically ordered
scenarios.description: Accounts are trimmed and lowercased and the target param is sorted (PROTOCOL §1). checkoutUrl() is offline and synchronous and exposes the canonical param.

scenarios.title: A target that does not exist is a configuration error (dev-time check)
scenarios.description: With dev checks on, the SDK looks the targets up once via GET /api/v1/targets and throws invalid_config because the target has exists: false. The SDK may throw from the constructor or from the first async operation; the group passes if the first step that throws throws invalid_config. No sign-in is started.

scenarios.title: The dev-time existence check runs at most once per process
scenarios.description: With dev checks on and existing targets, nothing throws and /targets is requested at most once, with both providers in one request.

scenarios.title: SPONSORKIT_DISABLE=1 turns the SDK into a no-op
scenarios.description: No network and no disk access, even with dev checks on. getFinancialContribution returns the disabled shape, nag.due() is false even when forced, and signIn/openCheckout reject with disabled.

scenarios.title: SPONSORKIT_DISABLE wins over mock mode
scenarios.description: With both mock and SPONSORKIT_DISABLE=1, the result is the disabled shape with mock: false.

scenarios.title: Mock preset "signed-out"
scenarios.description: mock: "signed-out" returns the expanded preset from fixtures/mock-presets.json without network or disk access.

scenarios.title: Mock preset "none"
scenarios.description: mock: "none" returns the expanded preset from fixtures/mock-presets.json without network or disk access.

scenarios.title: Mock preset "active-monthly"
scenarios.description: mock: "active-monthly" returns the expanded preset from fixtures/mock-presets.json without network or disk access.

scenarios.title: Mock preset "one-time"
scenarios.description: mock: "one-time" returns the expanded preset from fixtures/mock-presets.json without network or disk access.

scenarios.title: Mock preset "cancelled"
scenarios.description: mock: "cancelled" returns the expanded preset from fixtures/mock-presets.json without network or disk access.

scenarios.title: Mock preset "org"
scenarios.description: mock: "org" returns the expanded preset from fixtures/mock-presets.json without network or disk access.

scenarios.title: Mock preset "active-monthly" (opencollective target)
scenarios.description: mock: "active-monthly" returns the expanded preset from fixtures/mock-presets.json without network or disk access.

scenarios.title: SPONSORKIT_MOCK selects a preset
scenarios.description: The SPONSORKIT_MOCK environment variable takes the same preset names as the mock option.

scenarios.title: The mock option wins over SPONSORKIT_MOCK
scenarios.description: When both are set the constructor option is used.

scenarios.title: Custom mock contributions
scenarios.description: mock: { contributions } returns exactly those contributions with signedIn: true and the mock supporter.

scenarios.title: Unknown mock preset is a configuration error
scenarios.description: An unknown preset name throws invalid_config.

scenarios.title: Mock sign-in, checkout and sign-out are simulated in memory
scenarios.description: Starting from signed-out: signIn() resolves immediately and yields the empty signed-in shape; openCheckout() resolves immediately with a simulated contribution that later results include; signOut() returns to the signed-out shape. No network, no disk.

scenarios.title: Signed out: no network call
scenarios.description: A fresh SDK returns the signed-out result without contacting the API and without creating its storage file.

scenarios.title: Loopback sign-in
scenarios.description: signIn() binds 127.0.0.1:<random>, opens /connect with delivery=loopback, receives ?code= on /callback, exchanges it with its PKCE verifier, stores the session token and caches the token response's result. The next getFinancialContribution() is served from that cache.

scenarios.title: Paste-back sign-in
scenarios.description: signIn() with the paste method prints the /connect URL (delivery=paste, no redirect_uri) to stderr and calls promptForCode(). The test harness GETs that URL (the fake answers 200 text/plain whose body is the code) and returns the code. The SDK exchanges it.

scenarios.title: Provider sign-in denied
scenarios.description: The fake delivers ?error=access_denied to the loopback callback. signIn() rejects with SponsorkitError{code: "access_denied"}, does not call /auth/token and stores no token.

scenarios.title: Adding a second identity
scenarios.description: While signed in with GitHub, signIn({ provider: "opencollective" }) opens /connect with provider=opencollective&add=1 and sends the existing sessionToken to /auth/token. The new token holds both identities, and results include both providers' contributions.

scenarios.title: Sign-out deletes the token and cache locally
scenarios.description: signOut() makes no request (there is no server-side sign-out) and clears the stored token and cache. Afterwards the SDK is signed out and makes no requests.

steps.note: Simulates a new process: drop the SDK instance and create a new one from the last configure args.

scenarios.title: session_invalid clears the token and cache
scenarios.description: When /contributions answers 401 session_invalid, the SDK deletes token and cache and returns the signed-out result. It does not throw.

scenarios.title: Sponsorkit-Session renews the stored token
scenarios.description: The first /contributions response carries Sponsorkit-Session with a new token. The SDK replaces its stored token and uses the new one from then on, also after a restart.

steps.note: Simulates a new process: drop the SDK instance and create a new one from the last configure args.

scenarios.title: needsReconnect is passed through
scenarios.description: An identity whose provider token expired is returned with needsReconnect: true; the result is otherwise normal.

scenarios.title: Results are served from the local cache within cacheTtl
scenarios.description: After a refresh, getFinancialContribution() with the default cacheTtl (3600 s) makes no request and returns fromCache: true, stale: false. The cache survives a restart. cacheTtl: 0 always refreshes.

steps.note: Simulates a new process: drop the SDK instance and create a new one from the last configure args.

scenarios.title: A storage file written by another SDK is honoured
scenarios.description: The storage format is shared by all SDKs (PROTOCOL §8). A file with a fresh cache (storedAt = now) is served without a request.

scenarios.title: An expired cache is refreshed
scenarios.description: A cache whose storedAt is older than cacheTtl is not served; the SDK requests /contributions with the stored token.

scenarios.title: Network error with a cache returns the cache
scenarios.description: When the API is unreachable the SDK returns its cached result with fromCache: true and stale: true. It never throws and keeps the token.

scenarios.title: Network error without a cache returns an empty, stale, signed-in result
scenarios.description: Signed in (token on disk) but nothing cached and the API unreachable: the SDK returns the signed-in empty result with stale: true and does not throw.

scenarios.title: 5xx with a cache returns the cache
scenarios.description: A 503 from /contributions is treated like a network error: cached result, fromCache: true, stale: true, token kept.

scenarios.title: 5xx without a cache returns an empty, stale, signed-in result
scenarios.description: A 500 from /contributions and no cache: signed-in empty result with stale: true; no throw; token kept.

scenarios.title: Partial provider outage merges cached contributions
scenarios.description: /contributions reports unavailable: ["opencollective"] with stale: true and omits its contributions. The SDK fills in that provider's contributions from its cache and returns stale: true, fromCache: false.

scenarios.title: Partial outage without cached data for that provider
scenarios.description: If nothing is cached for the unavailable provider, only the available provider's contributions are returned, with stale: true.

scenarios.title: 429 rate_limited returns the cache and honours Retry-After
scenarios.description: /contributions answers 429 with Retry-After: 60. The SDK returns the cache (fromCache: true, stale: true), does not throw, and makes no further /contributions request for 60 s even with cacheTtl: 0 and even after the server stops rate limiting.

scenarios.title: 429 without a cache returns an empty, stale, signed-in result
scenarios.description: Rate limited and nothing cached: signed-in empty result with stale: true; no throw.

scenarios.title: Checkout detects a new contribution
scenarios.description: Signed in, openCheckout() opens /checkout (no challenge) which redirects to the provider. The SDK polls /contributions with cacheTtl 0; the second poll after the provider page was loaded contains a new contribution, and openCheckout resolves { status: "contributed", contribution }.

scenarios.title: Checkout detects a changed contribution
scenarios.description: A cancelled sponsorship that becomes active again (same id, changed status) counts as a result of the checkout.

scenarios.title: Checkout times out with status unknown
scenarios.description: Nothing changes; after `timeout` seconds openCheckout resolves { status: "unknown" } (no contribution). It never throws.

scenarios.title: Cancelling a checkout resolves status unknown
scenarios.description: The cancellation signal (AbortSignal / CancellationToken / context / ...) fires after 1.5 s; openCheckout stops polling and resolves { status: "unknown" } without throwing.

scenarios.title: Checkout while signed out signs in first (loopback)
scenarios.description: openCheckout() while signed out opens /checkout with challenge, delivery=loopback and redirect_uri. The fake delivers ?code= to the loopback callback, which redirects the browser to <apiBaseUrl>/checkout?<checkout params>&step=choose; the SDK exchanges the code, then polls until the new contribution appears.

scenarios.title: checkoutUrl() is synchronous and offline
scenarios.description: checkoutUrl() returns <apiBaseUrl>/checkout with the canonical targets and the given options, never a PKCE challenge, and makes no request.

scenarios.title: Nag run counting
scenarios.description: runs goes up by one per process per id on the first due() call. due() is true once runs >= every; shown() resets runs to 0 and sets lastShown. force: true bypasses the TTY/CI checks.

steps.note: Second call in the same process does not count another run.

scenarios.title: The nag predicate gates due() but runs still count
scenarios.description: With a false predicate due() is false even when runs >= every; runs are still counted. The predicate receives the current result.

scenarios.title: CI and SPONSORKIT_NO_NAG suppress nags unless forced
scenarios.description: Without force, due() is false when CI or SPONSORKIT_NO_NAG is set (and whenever stdout/stderr is not a TTY, as in test runners). force: true overrides these checks.

steps.note: The test process's stdout/stderr are not TTYs.

scenarios.title: orEvery makes a nag due after a duration since lastShown
scenarios.description: orEvery is an ISO-8601 duration. With lastShown null the duration clause is false. After shown(), due() becomes true once the duration has elapsed, regardless of runs.

scenarios.title: Storage directory 0700, files 0600
scenarios.description: The storage directory is created with mode 0700 and the storage file with 0600 (POSIX). Writes are atomic (temp file + rename), so no *.tmp files remain.

scenarios.title: Concurrent writers never corrupt the storage file
scenarios.description: Eight SDK instances (same storageDir) refresh concurrently, then eight record nag runs concurrently. The file is always valid JSON matching the storage schema, keeps the session token, and no *.tmp files remain. Lost nag increments are acceptable.

scenarios.title: Storage is keyed by targets_hash
scenarios.description: Instances with different target sets use different files (<targets_hash>.json) and do not share sessions.

scenarios.title: verifySession with matching targets
scenarios.description: verifySession(token, targets) calls /contributions with the token and returns the result when its targets equal the given set (after normalization and canonical ordering). It touches no storage.

scenarios.title: verifySession with mismatched targets throws
scenarios.description: The session is bound to github:sponsorkit-conformance only; verifying against both targets throws targets_mismatch.

scenarios.title: verifySession with an invalid session throws
scenarios.description: Unlike the client, the server helper throws session_invalid for a rejected token (and for a malformed one).
